title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page continues an elementary solving step in Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The setting is a rank-2 bundle M over a base S, with G = GL(M) (or SL). There are fixed sections ρ and σ; in the case of interest σ² = −1 with Tr σ = 0, and Tr ρ = 1, which looks like the order-4 and order-6 generators of SL2(Z). There is also a fixed element ε1 = ε1(1). The unknowns are a triple (ξ, η, μ), where μ is a scalar 'multiplier', satisfying a system (33)–(35). Eliminating η = ξ ε1 (1−μ) reduces the system to the conditions (36) on ξ: det ξ = 1, Tr(ξρ) = Tr ρ, and a third condition. The third condition is affine-linear in the entries of ξ and linear in μ, and reads P(ξ)μ − Q(ξ) = 0, as in (37)/(38). On the previous page the constant term was computed: −Q(ξ) = Tr(ξ ε1 σ) − Tr σ. Assuming (40 bis), ε1 = −λ0 ρ σ^{-1} with λ0 a central invertible scalar, this gives ε1 σ = −λ0 ρ. Then the second condition of (36) gives Tr(ξ ε1 σ) = −λ0 Tr(ξρ) = −λ0 Tr ρ. This page draws the conclusion: (41) Q(ξ) = c := λ0 Tr ρ + Tr σ, a constant independent of ξ. Grothendieck assumes (42) that c is everywhere invertible in O_S. He checks this in the case of interest: σ^{-1} = −σ, so ε1 = ρσ = −ρσ^{-1}, which gives λ0 = 1 and c = 1·1 + 0 = 1, 'ok'. The third equation then becomes (43) P(ξ)μ = c. Since c is a unit in a commutative ring, both P(ξ) and μ are units, and (44) μ = c/P(ξ). So μ is uniquely determined by ξ and is necessarily invertible. He then begins a Proposition, finished on the next page. Under (40 bis) and (42), the solutions (ξ, η, μ) correspond bijectively to sections ξ with det ξ = 1, Tr ξρ = Tr ρ and P(ξ) invertible, via (ξ, ξ ε1 (1−μ), c/P(ξ)). In effect this parametrises the solution scheme of the 'loop equation' system as an open subscheme (P ≠ 0) of a quadric-like subscheme of SL2.
errors: No mathematical errors. The sign bookkeeping is consistent: −Q = −λ0 Tr ρ − Tr σ gives Q = λ0 Tr ρ + Tr σ. The step 'P(ξ)μ = c with c a unit implies P(ξ) and μ are units' is correct over a commutative ring. The parenthetical check (λ0 = 1, c = 1) is consistent with Tr ρ = 1 and Tr σ = 0.
Minor notational slip in the image: '(37)' is crossed out and replaced by '(41)'. Some loose wording ('ξ1' versus 'ε1' in the transcription) is a transcription issue, not Grothendieck's.

ideas.what: Elimination of the auxiliary unknown μ: under a compatibility hypothesis ε1 = −λ0 ρ σ^{-1}, the constant term of the linear equation in μ becomes the constant c = λ0 Tr ρ + Tr σ. Hence μ = c/P(ξ) is unique and invertible, and solutions correspond to an open subscheme of {det ξ = 1, Tr ξρ = Tr ρ}.
ideas.modern_name: explicit parametrisation of a solution scheme in SL2 (elimination of variables / open subscheme description)
ideas.usually_credited_to: routine linear algebra; context relates to Grothendieck–Teichmüller / SL2(Z) generators of orders 4 and 6
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) treats related themes, but this specific computation appears unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: A routine elimination step in a matrix-equation computation; there is no new concept or connection on this page beyond its archival context.
